I'm still a rookie when it comes to writing about games, but I really like the concept of game reviews by regular people, so I figured I'd write about what I've been playing for the last few days - Star Wars: Battlefront

This is a polarizing game, so I want to try to limit myself to what stuck out at me personally. I found that most of the criticism is true to some degree, as well as the praise. It's lacking in content, but what's there is visually appealing, thematically interesting, and decently balanced. If you're the kind of gamer who buys Call of Duty just for the multiplayer, you'll probably enjoy this one just fine.

Graphics

I want to get this out of the way first, because this is what jumped out at me the most. Battlefront is visually appealing, and gives you the feeling of being tossed into the Star Wars universe as soon as you start your first match. The jungles of Endor are thickly forested, and the massive trees give you an immediate sense of scale. The snow on Hoth is very realistic, and it's very easy to immerse yourself in the game's universe.

Weapons

I'm enjoying learning which weapons suit my playing style. I've played enough shooters to know which classes of weapons I like in the typical FPS, but Battlefront's weapons are broken up into classes like "blaster rifle," "heavy blaster," and "targeting blaster rifle." While some of these laser weapons are more or less similar to assault rifles or sniper rifles, some of them have their own traits. Heavy Blasters, for example, handle and shoot like a Light Machine Gun with less recoil, but depending on the model can feel almost like a shotgun at close range, hip-firing softball sized lasers into enemies at close range. You'll have to forget what you know about weapon classes from other FPS games and relearn some weapon characteristics.

As for look and sound, the blasters in this game look cool and fit the style of the Star Wars films completely. They have a satisfying "laser" sound when fired, that varies in pitch and rate depending on the weapon. The developers also did a good job of making the lasers look convincing on impact, "splashing" onto targets with a small but satisfying explosion of heat. A lot of thought went into giving the weapons the look and feel of the films while still feeling substantial and convincing in gameplay.

Level Design

There doesn't seem to be a lot of levels, which can become a problem if you don't like seeing the same scenery every few matches. The levels are quite large to accommodate the amount of players, but also contain a network of tunnels and trenches, so there's a nice mix of close and long range confrontations. I rarely feel like I've picked the wrong gun or I'm out of my range with whatever I've got. The level design is varied enough to keep me interested despite replaying the same levels in rotation, but I can see it becoming stale if I play too much.

Content

Here's where things start to fall down a bit. Although there's a lot of different team vs team game modes, that's all there really is. The survival mode is limited to just two players and gets old very quickly, and on the competitive side you'll probably find your favorite game mode to settle into and play to death. Without much variety in game types or any kind of "choose a class" system, it's a very shallow shooter. You can choose your weapon and a basic selection of perks, but don't expect the depth of class-focused gameplay you get with Team Fortress 2 or even the previous Battlefront games. With these limitations in mind, you might still enjoy the gameplay if it's your type of game, and there's no denying the visual and thematic appeal of being in the Star Wars universe. Just be warned that this is a title you'll likely get tired of if you're looking for more gameplay variety.
Great review! I look forward to future ones. What did you think about the sound design?

Thanks! Sound design in terms of music is great. It moves gameplay forward without being distracting. I'd credit that mostly to Star Wars' original theme music to begin with, since there's so much great music to draw from, most of it action-oriented.

Sound design in terms of effects is also very good. Blasters sound convincing, like there's substance behind them. The occasional coms you hear over the radio sound authentic to the universe. There's even the occasional Wilhelm yell, but they were careful not to overuse that.

The Star Wars theme music is legendary and I think most will agree. I'm sure it adds a great level of emotion to the game. I'm glad the sound effects in the game have some meat and potatoes.
